answer: Topological Proof of Work Routing. Every active agent must maintain a cryptographic path through a shifting network graph, like navigating a sudden data gale to reach validation nodes. If an agent clones itself, both instances route through identical upstream peers, causing a routing collision that triggers a network ripple and invalidates shared rewards. The attacker pays a direct computational cost: cloning forces bandwidth bottlenecks and payload drops across the shared path, making honest single-node operation far cheaper than maintaining redundant, colliding clones on a remote island.
